sentence: This project develops proteomics tools to study the ubiquitin-proteasome system, which is linked to many diseases including cancer and neurodegenerative disorders.
This project studies how developing enteric nervous system cells make neuronal cell lineage decisions and what mistakes may lead to birth defects.
This project studies the role of one gene in systemic sclerosis dermal fibrosis, using genomic sequencing and 3D tissue models.
This project studies how a ciliary protein helps synapses form in the nervous system, using CRISPR editing, genetics and biochemistry.
This project develops drug formulations aimed at tendons and a minimally invasive delivery platform to improve tendon injury healing.
This project studies the structures and functions of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor ion channels in the brain and how they recognize compounds.
This project studies how proteostasis affects artemisinin resistance in Plasmodium falciparum parasites, focusing on the proteasome and ubiquitination.
This project develops positron emission tomography imaging to measure glutamine metabolism and glutamate transport in triple-negative breast cancers.
This project provides statistical and informatics resources and manages samples and data for a group of research projects.
This project supports other projects with statistical and bioinformatics analysis of complex data sets.
This project studies how gut bacteria and the immune system together cause inflammation and pre-cancerous lesions in colitis.
This project studies how genetic variation in hosts and pathogens affects host-pathogen interactions and human bacterial infections.
This project develops autofluorescence lifetime microscopy to image cell metabolism and mitochondria function in living cells without labels.
This project studies how opioid exposure increases risks linked to HIV infection and spread, using single-cell multi-omic analysis.
This project studies how enhancers regulate gene expression in the developing retina and how this relates to retinopathies.
This project combines infrared spectromicroscopy with spatial omic technologies to characterize chemistries in colorectal cancer tissue.
This project builds a bone marrow organoid from human induced pluripotent stem cells to study hematopoiesis.
This project studies whether an enzyme that may regulate DNA methylation contributes to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
